Gudde, N., Larivé, J.-F. and Yugo, M. (2019). Refinery 2050: Conceptual Assessment. Exploring opportunities and challenges for the EU refining industry to transition towards a low-CO2 intensive economy. Concawe Report no. 9/19, Brussels, September 2019. Prepared for the Concawe Special Task Force Refinery 2050 (STF-2). Appendixes published separately as report 9/19A.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 2; front matter roman I-IV). Main file: per-pathway capital intensities of Table 6.2.9-2 (HVO co-processing, unit conversion, stand-alone; stand-alone and refinery BTL; refinery pyrolysis+HDT; refinery HDT for bio-oil; stand-alone and refinery e-fuel), converted from M EUR/(kt-liq/a) to EUR/(t/a) (the EUR/kW-liq figures are in the notes); Sect. 5 text capex for dedicated HVO, lipid co-processing pretreatment, BTL (>5 G EUR per Mt/a), e-fuel plants (M EUR per t/d, 400 t/d plant, production cost 2500-3000 EUR/t); e-fuel electricity per t product derived from Table 5.4.3-1 and the 350-400 MWe / 400 t/d example; electrolytic H2 capex 2.6 M EUR/(kt/a). Flows: mass balances of Table 6.2.9-1 and Table 13.4-1 (printed per 100 t feed, written per t feed with formula), lipid diesel yields (83% co-processing, 81% HC conversion), BTL wax and diesel yields, pyrolysis-oil road-fuel yield, e-fuel CO2 and H2 demand. Other-values: whole-refinery RafXl results per case (Sect. 13: crude, products, gas and electricity imports, H2 by route, captured CO2, site CO2 per t product), EU-wide Table 9.3-1 (an image, read from the rendered page), scale notes. Not loaded: whole-refinery cases in the main file (internal fuel gas and coke not printed, so only imported energy is known); the 19/22% efficiency gains, grid factors (Table 4-1), capture energy 1.1/8.1 GJ/t CO2, capture caps and 70% electrolyser efficiency, all reprinted from Concawe 8/19 (concawe_2019_001); figures without printed values (5.2.2-1, 5.3.2.3-1, 5.3.3.3-1, 5.4.2-1, 10-1, plant utilisation, emissions); LBST e-fuel cost quotes; biomass and algae availability (mostly reprinted from Ecorys 2017). No measures file (no efficiency measures with numbers beyond 8/19). Prices: no price year stated; EUR, publication year 2019 used. Traps: Sect. 5.2.3 prints "EUR 0.05 per kt/a" for lipid pretreatment capex (read as M EUR); Sect. 13 site-emission rows are labelled "t/kt liq prod" but are t CO2/t; Table 6.2.9-1 O2, char, C3+C4 and Heavy FT rows have blank cells, columns assigned by layout and checked by mass closure (each pathway balances to within 0.1); Table 6.2.9-2 capital costs stated +/-50%; plants assumed 85% utilisation and product LHV 44 GJ/t. PDF metadata title is wrong (a different Word document); title page confirms report 9/19.
